question.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[-2,2]\times [-2,2]⊆{R}^{2},$ where $$ f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-{y}^{3}-1 \\ {y}^{2}-2x\end{aligned}]. $$ Calculate one iteration of the Newton-Raphson process that starts with ${x}_{0}=[-1,\,1]^{T}.$
${x}_{1}=[$ {{field-1}} $]$
$0.2$
question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-{y}^{3}-1) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-{y}^{3}-1) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2}-2x) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}-2x)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x & -3{y}^{2} \\ -2 & 2y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}2x & -3{y}^{2} \\ -2 & 2y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-{y}^{3}-1 \\ {y}^{2}-2x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-{[\begin{aligned}2x & -3{y}^{2} \\ -2 & 2y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-{y}^{3}-1 \\ {y}^{2}-2x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}2(-1) & -3(1)^{2} \\ -2 & 2(1)\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}(-1)^{2}-(1)^{3}-1 \\ (1)^{2}-2(-1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{(-2)\cdot 2-(-3)\cdot (-2)}[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-0.3 \\ 0.2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
